key_insight: A foundation-model-based, data-efficient pipeline can detect duodenal epithelial neoplasia in whole-slide biopsy images with strong cross-hospital generalizability despite few rare-tumour cases.
clinical_relevance: This could help pathology workflows flag rare duodenal neoplasms earlier and more consistently, especially where annotated training data are limited.
method: 5-hospital H&E duodenal biopsy WSI dataset (8,027 normal; 401 neoplastic) at 10x
Patch embeddings from the Hibou-B foundation model with site-specific standardisation
PCA + Gaussian mixture model + Random Forest classifier, evaluated with leave-one-hospital-out and external testing
evidence_signal: Performance was 90% mean accuracy (AUC 0.96) in leave-one-hospital-out validation and 94% accuracy (AUC 0.97) on an independent external hospital test set.
watch_item: Results come from a retrospective, multi-centre dataset and need prospective validation before routine deployment across broader lab settings.
paper_title: Data-efficient machine learning for the detection of duodenal neoplasia: a multi-centre study
